quote_text:
What were your thoughts on your  team's display there today?
Overall pretty good. Quite dominant.  Felt quite comfortable out there. Um,  
don't mean to disrespect Aberdeen in any way,  but I don't really feel like they were able to  
create any sort of threat. Maybe two or three  occasions, but even that wasn't really… I felt  
quite comfortable in the back line. Um, I think  going forward in the first half we needed to do  
more. Had a few good chances, but overall  we also needed to create a lot more, which  
we have then done in the second half. And then  it can be quite delightful and quite enjoyable,  
I think, watching us— which we haven't done enough  throughout the season. Not consistently enough.  
Um, but on the back of not having won here  for seven games I think, and also not being  
able to keep a clean sheet in quite a while,  I think that was overall a satisfying display.
Were those two things— the lack of home  victories and the lack of clean sheets  
recently— were they two things that have been  discussed internally in the changing room?
It's been addressed. Um, I mean the gaffer, he's a  proper Ranger. I think he bleeds blue and, um, he  
makes sure that he gives us those little pointers  because these things are important. If you play  
for this club, these things are what the support  cares about. Um, so he definitely made a point of  
addressing it without overstressing it really, but  he just made sure that we don't forget about it.
Sterling man— how much have you seen  him grow as a teammate this season?
A lot. Because I remember around this time  of the year last season, maybe a bit earlier,  
he just came off the back of an injury, I think,  and he struggled a bit just to find his rhythm  
and to get minutes as well. Um, and then if you  see the player that he grew into this season— um,  
fair play to him. It's not easy. Um, especially  if we are on such a rocky ride that we have been  
on this season. Um, but I think he's grown a  lot. Um, and it's impressive really. It's just  
important, I think, to keep the bigger picture  in mind, 'cause he's still young. Um, I think if  
he carries on like that, there's a real player in  him, there's loads for him to look forward to. Um,  
and I think he's been a joy for many people this  season, especially towards the end of the season.  
And he carried a few niggles here and there,  went through it. Um, so yeah, delighted for him.
He's been spoken of as somebody that one future  depends— James could perhaps be a future captain  
here. Do you see that kind of characteristic in  him— somebody who can be a proper leader in Niko?
Yeah, I think. Not trying to bash him, but I  think he's still young. Um, there's probably  
still a few things he has to learn, which  is only normal. Um, 'cause I think— I mean,  
I can't look into his mind, but I think that as  much as it's enjoyable, it's quite a lot for him  
to process as well. And I mean, if you get man  of the match pretty much every week, the whole  
stadium sings your songs, it does get you excited  sometimes. And, um, maybe you lose track a little  
bit of things going on around you. But again,  it's a process and that's normal. I think a lot  
of good players have been through that. But he  definitely has a lot of qualities— if you just  
see his energy on the pitch, the way he's trying  to demand of players around him. Um, definitely.
You say Leon is still young— do you think  he can go further in the game? High hopes?
Further in the game as in  how far? Or… you tell me.
How far can he go?
It depends. I mean, I think he showed his  quality in Europe, which is always interesting  
for teams in Europe. Um, like I said, there  is a player in him. There's probably things  
he will have to learn. It probably would help  him if he scores a few more goals. But again,  
he came from a rough patch in terms of injuries,  and I think he made not just one, probably two  
or three massive steps forward. So I think the  doors are open for him to reach… what do you say,  
higher— higher height is probably wrong,  huh? But greater heights— that's the one.
A lot of change coming over the summer— I'm not  quite sure what's happening with the squad— and  
as you look ahead to midweek and potentially this  being your last game here, what are your emotions?
Uh, I try not to think about it too much.  Um, I'm quite relaxed, to be honest. But  
maybe that's just who I am. Um, I can be  very, very emotional. Um, but I will— well,  
I will keep that for the moment where I have  certainty, which I don't have at the moment.
So sure, you are still hoping that perhaps it  could be a place here— it's written in the stars?
I trust the big man upstairs. And some  people up here in the club. So we'll see.
Even at 37, you’ve shown this season you can still  be, you know, an effective player for this team.
I think so. I mean, without trying to sound  arrogant, but age is nothing but a number.  
I've looked after myself throughout my whole  career pretty well, I would like to think. Um,  
which is the reason why I can still perform  at this level. Um, if I would feel that I  
start to really struggle, I would admit  it. But I absolutely do not feel that way.  
Um, felt even at times this season and even  last season, I trained more than ever. Because I  
remember when I was around 22, 23, and I played  with some senior players— there was only one,  
I think— Michael Tarnat, you might remember him. I  think he was 37 at the time. It was my first year  
as a pro. He was managed here and there. And all  the other ones around 29, 30, 31, 32— they were  
all managed. And I was always saying to my best  friend back then, "I can't wait for them days, you  
know, when I don't have to do the full training  week." But not for me. Apparently times have  
changed. But I've adapted and, um, yeah, long may  it continue. Um, and just have to do what I can on  
the pitch and off the pitch to keep my fitness.  And I think I've found my recipe to do that.
Do you sense an excitement that's  coming because of the changes this  
summer? Would you like to be part of that new era?
Yeah. I mean, it's exciting. Um, it's going  to be challenging as well, I think. Because  
we have a— where is it? I thought there’s a  big batch— there's a big badge! We have a big  
badge to uphold. And I think in recent years,  we've probably done more to lower it a bit.  
And we need to put it high again. And I think  it's not a light match, as we all know. Um,  
but if I can be part of a group that kind  of polishes it again and lifts it up again,  
of course. Because I said it last year I think,  or maybe the last time I was— or before I left  
the first time— that this has become my club  now. Because I never really supported a team  
die hard. And if, like I said, if I can be part of  a refurbish— I think you say— then I'd sign that.
Last couple— are you prepared to wait, Leon?  Obviously people are saying they want decisions,  
you want to know what’s coming—  but are you prepared to wait to  
find out if you're going to have a future?
I think I have no choice. That’s one. And I'm  very blessed that my father from a young age  
taught me the value of patience. So I'm  just going to have patience, as always,  
as I've had all my life with many things. Um,  and then I just— I have to see what's happening.
When do you expect to be informed of  the club's decision? Is that something—
Um, it's hard to say. Because like I said, it's  not in my control. I don't know at what stage  
the whole thing is. I mean, they're on the search  for a manager— are they? I don't really know. So,  
um, not my business really.  Until it becomes mine. Hopefully.
In terms of— you've been told when the club are  
going to sit you down as players  and inform you what happens next?
Like I said, I don't know  if there are any deadlines.  
I can't say. I would tell you, but I can't.
Leon, if it's not meant to be— you mentioned  you’ve been a Rangers fan— now if it’s not  
meant to be, you have to leave this summer,  how would you reflect on your time at Rangers?
Um, I think I've won everything domestically,  if I'm not mistaken, which I'm proud of. Um,  
I would like to think— or I hope— I would be  remembered as somebody who played his heart  
out all the time. Because I think that's just how  I'm built. Um, like I said, proud but also humble,  
because I know there’s been many players before  me who have achieved a lot more. And I think you  
always have to put things into perspective. But,  um, definitely the best time of my career. I said  
it before once, that I wish I would have been in  an environment where you’re just expected to win  
all the time a lot earlier in my career— 'cause  I don't know, maybe I would have ended up at  
Real Madrid. Who knows. I don't know. That’s for  you to decide. But, um, no, I've really enjoyed  
every single second. The good times. Also the bad  times. Um, and yeah, it's— it's become family.
title: "This has become my club" | Leon Balogun Post Match Press Conference | Rangers 4-0 Aberdeen
